I'm sorry, but that question doesn't tell me enough about your tastes to give a reasonable answer. First off, what system(s) are you looking for? Mobile is a whole lot different than PC or Console. Second, what type of gaming experience do you prefer? Do you like high action, or games that let you set your own pace? Open world, or directed experience? Games that challenge your mind, or your skills? How much time do you want to put into the game? A few minutes at a time, an hour or so, or a long gaming session?

Without any of this context, I'm going to have to suggest Fantasy World Dizzy.

Suggestions:

Garry's mod - If you like inventing things. It's a pretty sweet physics sandbox if you can figure out how to use the tools well (I've got ADHD and over 2000 hours on it (if you include gmod 9 before steam tracked stats)).

Modded Minecraft (if you have the RAM). Seriously, I must have hundreds of hours logged on each mod let alone the base game.

Factorio - The pace is pretty good so long as you can make it a few minutes in the beginning. The constant attacks and need to expand your resource production makes it hard to get bored playing.

These last few will be a bit of an acquired taste:

Dungeon Crawl Stone Soup - Roguelike of all Roguelikes in my humble opinion. It's got hardcore detail if you want to learn all the things, it's easy enough to pick up and get started (with a hotkey cheat-sheet), and there's a pretty decent variety of ways to make your character.

Dwarf Fortress - Has a learning curve like an inverted cliff-face strewn with dead corpses of others who tried to overcome it but failed. But if you want a game that you can Never Ever EVER see everything in, Dwarf Fortress is for you. I'd explain more but.. It's just so huge. Best I can say is it's a very accurate simulation of a randomly generated fantasy world. And you control one man on an adventure, or manage a sim-city like fortress of hardy dwarves. (Hint: "Use the Lazy Newb Pack")
